What is the total cost (in Rs.) of levelling the entire park at the rate of Rs. 80 per square metre, if the breadth of the rectangle is 10 m?( in integer value) (use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Rectangle: breadth = 10 m, length = 3 × 10 = 30 m
Area of rectangle = 30 × 10 = 300

Four semicircles → 2 pairs

Pair 1 (on length): diameter = 10 → radius = 5 → forms 1 full circle
Area = 25π

Pair 2 (on breadth): diameter = 30 → radius = 15 → forms 1 full circle
Area = 225π

Total added area = 25π + 225π = 250π
Using π = 22/7 → 250 × 22/7 = 785.714

Total area = 300 + 785.714 = 1085.714

Cost = 1085.714 × 80 = 86857.12

questions.question: Read the following statement and identify the correct inference(s). Statement: "The civic authority has urged citizens to use public transport instead of private vehicles to reduce the severe smog covering the city." Inferences: I. Private vehicles are a major contributor to the smog in the city. II. Public transport produces zero pollution. III. The civic authority believes citizens will comply with the request.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement and identify the correct inference(s).
Statement: "The civic authority has urged citizens to use public transport instead of private vehicles to reduce the severe smog covering the city."
Inferences:
I. Private vehicles are a major contributor to the smog in the city.
II. Public transport produces zero pollution.
III. The civic authority believes citizens will comply with the request.
questions.solution:
I. Private vehicles are a major contributor to the smog in the city. (Correct) The statement explicitly links the use of private vehicles to the smog. By asking citizens to switch to public transport to reduce the smog, the authority is identifying private vehicle emissions as a significant cause of the problem.

II. Public transport produces zero pollution. (Incorrect) This is an extreme generalization. While public transport is generally more efficient per passenger and can help reduce overall city pollution, the statement does not claim it produces "zero" pollution. It only implies that it is the better alternative in this context.

III. The civic authority believes citizens will comply with the request. (Correct) In logical reasoning, when an authority issues an "urge" or "appeal," it is based on the underlying assumption (or belief) that the target audience is capable of following the advice and that the request will have some effect. If they believed no one would listen, they wouldn't issue the urge.

Paradoxically, this explosion of available knowledge has made the older model of education less effective, not more. As a result, learners may graduate with impressive grades but limited capacity to navigate complex real-world problems. Rather than simply delivering answers, teachers design experiences that invite questioning, experimentation, and reflection. In this view, mistakes are not signs of failure but stepping stones towards deeper insight. Learning becomes less about memorising a fixed body of knowledge and more about developing a flexible toolkit for engaging with an unpredictable world. For centuries, education was likened to the filling of an empty vessel: students were seen as passive recipients into whom teachers poured facts, dates, and formulas. This model suited an era in which information was scarce and authority was centralised. In such a world, knowing more than others could secure privilege, power, and stability. However, in the digital age, information is not only abundant but overwhelming. With a few keystrokes, a learner can access more data than entire libraries once contained. Paradoxically, this explosion of available knowledge has made the older model of education less effective, not more.

Today, the challenge is no longer access to information but the ability to evaluate, connect, and apply it. Employers increasingly value skills such as critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration over the mere possession of facts. Yet many education systems still reward students primarily for reproducing information in high-stakes examinations. As a result, learners may graduate with impressive grades but limited capacity to navigate complex real-world problems.

A more responsive model of education treats the learner as an active participant in constructing understanding. Rather than simply delivering answers, teachers design experiences that invite questioning, experimentation, and reflection. In this view, mistakes are not signs of failure but stepping stones towards deeper insight. Learning becomes less about memorising a fixed body of knowledge and more about developing a flexible toolkit for engaging with an unpredictable world.

Q- Which of the following words is the most appropriate synonym of "overwhelming" as used in the passage:
questions.solution:
✅ Option: Intimidating

Explanation:

In the passage, “overwhelming” is used to describe the sheer volume and excess of information available in the digital age, which can be difficult to process or manage.
